title: What People Would Give up to Live Longer — Survey
paragraphs: If you could give something up to get 10 extra years of healthy life, what would it be?
That's what National Geographic tried to find out in a new survey of 1,000 US adults, asking people about their views on aging.

It found that most people actually care more about staying healthy than just living longer. In fact, almost two-thirds of Americans said they would rather live a shorter, healthier life than a longer one with health problems.
The survey also asked people what they would give up to enjoy 10 more years of healthy life.

The most popular answer was alcohol, chosen by 35%. Next came social media, named by 26%. That was followed by sugar at 23%, and caffeine at 22%. Fifteen percent said they'd give up their favorite food or their career. But only 13% would give up their car!
One in 10 even said they would give up their partner — while one in five said they wouldn't give up anything at all.
However, nearly two-thirds worried that if they lived longer, they wouldn't have enough money — and only 16% said they would retire later to get 10 extra years.
But if people could live healthy lives after 120, 29% said they would be OK with retiring after 70.
And 41% said it would benefit society if we could live more than 150 years, because we could keep so many people's knowledge for longer.
However, one-quarter said living so long wouldn't benefit society, and worried it would hurt the economy and lead to the world having too many people.
